page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include a GPU and relies on 1 GB of network-attached local storage, which represents a design tradeoff for workloads requiring high-capacity local disk space.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The AMD EPYC processor achieves a top-tier rating in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and a strong rating in multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with large-block read and write operations reaching top-tier speeds of 530.35 GB/sec and 259.87 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions and physics simulations, place this server in the top 10% of tested systems.

This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive and multi-threaded applications such as database operations, where it achieves top-tier Passmark database scores, and Redis key-value stores, processing 111.5 million operations per second. It also supports CPU-based machine learning tasks, demonstrating top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds on small LLM models. The dedicated resource allocation offers high compute density and predictable performance, making it a cost-effective option for enterprise-scale web serving, data processing, and parallelized compilation tasks without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware.
